prs.title: fix(server): reject concurrent duplicate JSON-RPC request ids
prs.author: arimu1
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs address the same underlying bug in _handle_post_request: the server keys the in-flight `_request_streams` map by request id without rejecting collisions, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key get cross-wired (one receives the other's response, or hangs). #3063 adds a straightforward `if request_id in self._request_streams` check using the existing `str(message.id)` key and returns 400 on collision. #3221 covers the same scenario but replaces the key scheme itself with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` helper, fixing two edge cases #3063's plain `str(id)` approach still leaves open: (1) JSON-RPC id `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) are distinct per spec but both stringify to the same key, so #3063 would falsely 409 a legitimate string id colliding with an in-flight int id of the same digits; (2) a JSON-RPC string id equal to the literal `"_GET_stream"` sentinel would collide with the standalone GET stream slot under #3063's scheme. #3221's key format (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) prevents both. (2 PRs)

prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2492 fixes this by persisting `oauth_metadata` through two new `TokenStorage` protocol methods, but both default to no-op/`None` ('Optional: no-op by default' per the added docstring) — so the fix only takes effect for storage backends that implement the new methods, leaving the bug unfixed for any existing/third-party storage implementation that doesn't opt in. #3241's `_discover_oauth_metadata` instead performs the discovery inline via yielded httpx requests immediately before the eager refresh (and reuses it on the 401 path too), so it closes the gap for every storage backend without requiring any interface changes downstream.

prs.title: fix(oauth): avoid lock contention for long-running requests
prs.author: ctaylor86
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: `context.lock` is held across the full `async_auth_flow` generator including long-running yielded requests (e.g. SSE long-polls), blocking unrelated concurrent requests through the same OAuth provider; both PRs split the single lock into a broad state lock plus a dedicated single-flight refresh lock. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: `context.lock` is held across the full `async_auth_flow` generator including long-running yielded requests (e.g. SSE long-polls), blocking unrelated concurrent requests through the same OAuth provider; both PRs split the single lock into a broad state lock plus a dedicated single-flight refresh lock. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2858 keeps `context.lock` as an `anyio.Lock`. #3243 switches both locks to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` and its own added comment explains why: httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, and `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release on the trio backend, which would raise at runtime under that cross-task resumption. #2858 does not address this task-ownership case, so it can still fail on the trio backend in the exact concurrent-request scenario both PRs are trying to fix.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both PRs address the same underlying bug in _handle_post_request: the server keys the in-flight `_request_streams` map by request id without rejecting collisions, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key get cross-wired (one receives the other's response, or hangs). #3063 adds a straightforward `if request_id in self._request_streams` check using the existing `str(message.id)` key and returns 400 on collision. #3221 covers the same scenario but replaces the key scheme itself with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` helper, fixing two edge cases #3063's plain `str(id)` approach still leaves open: (1) JSON-RPC id `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) are distinct per spec but both stringify to the same key, so #3063 would falsely 409 a legitimate string id colliding with an in-flight int id of the same digits; (2) a JSON-RPC string id equal to the literal `"_GET_stream"` sentinel would collide with the standalone GET stream slot under #3063's scheme. #3221's key format (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) prevents both.

clusters.pick_reason: #2858 keeps `context.lock` as an `anyio.Lock`. #3243 switches both locks to `anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1)` and its own added comment explains why: httpx can resume or close an auth-flow generator from a different task than the one that acquired the lock, and `anyio.Lock` enforces same-task acquire/release on the trio backend, which would raise at runtime under that cross-task resumption. #2858 does not address this task-ownership case, so it can still fail on the trio backend in the exact concurrent-request scenario both PRs are trying to fix.

Consolidate onto #3221 and close #3063.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both PRs address the same underlying bug in _handle_post_request: the server keys the in-flight `_request_streams` map by request id without rejecting collisions, so two concurrent requests that map to the same key get cross-wired (one receives the other's response, or hangs). #3063 adds a straightforward `if request_id in self._request_streams` check using the existing `str(message.id)` key and returns 400 on collision. #3221 covers the same scenario but replaces the key scheme itself with a type-preserving `_request_stream_key()` helper, fixing two edge cases #3063's plain `str(id)` approach still leaves open: (1) JSON-RPC id `1` (int) and `"1"` (string) are distinct per spec but both stringify to the same key, so #3063 would falsely 409 a legitimate string id colliding with an in-flight int id of the same digits; (2) a JSON-RPC string id equal to the literal `"_GET_stream"` sentinel would collide with the standalone GET stream slot under #3063's scheme. #3221's key format (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) prevents both.
